frequency_question: What proportion of regulatory review cycles under elevated credit-to-GDP gap or systemic vulnerability conditions result in a non-zero CCyB activation within a given 16-month horizon?
membership_rule: Members include all national macroprudential authorities possessing the mandate to set a CCyB during periods where financial stability frameworks are active (2016-present). Excluded are jurisdictions without an operational CCyB framework or emerging markets lacking standardized implementation data.

cases.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB Activation 2019
Bank of England CCyB Rate Restoration 2022

provenance_note: claims 40 cases from only 7 named (5.7x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 6 named representative peer events; estimated total population of comparable G20 tightening actions is approximately 15 instances across 40 observed country-years.
known_gaps: Excludes minor emerging market adjustments where regulatory reporting transparency is variable.
skeleton: G20 jurisdictions with active macroprudential mandates evaluated across biannual policy review windows over 10 years, yielding approximately 50 distinct national implementation periods where systemic indicators crossed monitoring thresholds.
multiplier: 6 positive activations identified across major peer jurisdictions out of roughly 40 applicable monitoring cycles where credit gaps were moderately positive.
validity_reason: Macroprudential frameworks and Basel III capital rules remain stable across this horizon, preserving the base rate applicability.
